## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

The *Pakkagodhajātaka* (Ja 333), translated as "The Cooked Lizard", is a canonical story preserved in the Jātaka collection of the Pali canon [SuttaCentral]. According to the narrative framework recorded in the commentary, the Buddha told this story while staying at Jetavana regarding a certain landowner [SuttaCentral]. In the core verse edited by V. Fausböll, a queen addresses the royal king (*rathesabha*), stating that his true character was recognized in the midst of the forest when a roasted monitor lizard escaped on the branch of an *assattha* tree (*assatthadumasākhāya pakkagodhā palāyathā 'ti*) [Fausböll 1883]. The commentary explains the verse in detail, glossing *tirīṭino* and clarifying that *pakkā* means roasted over embers (*aṅgārapakkā*) [Fausböll 1883].

Regarding parallels and text reuse, SuttaCentral records the *Puṭabhattajātaka* (Ja 223) as a passage-level parallel [SuttaCentral]. Textual reuse across these related narratives is confirmed by DharmaNexus, which identifies multiple matching passages with the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā*, particularly across segments §1.6–3.4 aligning with both the second division (Dutiyo bhāgo §1293–1297) and third division (Tatiyo bhāgo §857_1–863) [DharmaNexus]. Beyond Pali literature, DharmaNexus detects eight cross-language alignments with the Sanskrit *Mahāvastu-avadāna* with plausibility scores up to 95 [DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral records four translations of the text in four modern languages [SuttaCentral].
